== module-switch-procedure
# A module's switch: variant generations, the C's Rust library, and the C test gate

Status: `open`.

## Signal

Procedures worked out by hand that the skills should state, met at the campaign's first
switch from C (`modules/libgit2/src/util/utf8.c/integration/run-1`), which every later switch
repeats, and two gaps where following the skills as written fails:

1. **The variants cannot be rebuilt in place.** `porting-workflow`'s Builds section rebuilds
   the shared variants "from the C that remains once the integration lands", and
   `testing-builds` has them prebuilt and immutable. Each variant's `configure` takes the C
   from the base checkout (`cmake -S ../../../c`), whose `c/` the batches still running hold
   with the module as C: three agents were building and testing against
   `crustify/builds` while this switch ran. A build configured from the integration
   worktree's `c/` instead is bound to a tree that is purged once the module integrates,
   and its build files then name sources that no longer exist.
2. **Campaign mode cannot build the Rust library the C links.** The C consumers link "the
   safe crate's Rust static library, built in campaign mode so that it carries no C of its
   own", but campaign mode (`bindgen`, Build modes) requires the variant's artifacts and
   static archive, which exist only once the C has linked, and the C's link needs the Rust
   library first. Once the C links it, the link edges campaign mode reads list it among
   their libraries, so the Rust tests would link the Rust twice, once from their rlib and once
   from the library.

# An export whose failure needs an outcome a panic cannot give

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent works around: `porting-symbols`' Functions section has a panic caught at an
export's gateway "reported as a failure, or aborts where the function cannot fail", and a
function can fail through a convention that a panic leaves no way to follow.

## Evidence

`wave-186/batch-5/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) exported `cli_opt_parse` and
`cli_opt_parser_next`. Both report their failures through a status and the outcome they write
to the caller's `cli_opt`: the CLI's commands then call `cli_opt_usage_error(cmd, opts,
&invalid_opt)`, which describes that outcome, its spec and argument. A panic in the parse
leaves no outcome to write: a zeroed one with a failing status would make the CLI print
`unknown option: (null)` for an argument that was never unknown. Both gateways abort on a
panic instead, documented on each. `cli_opt_foreach`, whose failure is a bare non-zero
`int` its caller (`common.c`) only tests, reports a panic as `-1`. The rule, read literally,
asks for the failure in all three; the batch departed from it for two.

## Destination

# A port batch runs its module's tests with its exports linked in place of its C

Status: `open`.

One procedure repeated by hand, which no gate runs. `testing-gates`' Regressions section
has a `port` batch check and lint the safe crate with its module's export feature on,
"which compiles the module's gateway without linking it", and compare each export's
signature with its raw binding. Nothing runs the gateway before the module's switch: every
gate builds with the feature off, and the `testing` skill puts an export's tests "with the

== module-switch-procedure
# A module's switch: variant generations, the C's Rust library, and the C test gate

Status: `open`.

## Signal

Procedures worked out by hand that the skills should state, met at the campaign's first
switch from C (`modules/libgit2/src/util/utf8.c/integration/run-1`), which every later switch
repeats, and two gaps where following the skills as written fails:

1. **The variants cannot be rebuilt in place.** `porting-workflow`'s Builds section rebuilds
   the shared variants "from the C that remains once the integration lands", and
   `testing-builds` has them prebuilt and immutable. Each variant's `configure` takes the C
   from the base checkout (`cmake -S ../../../c`), whose `c/` the batches still running hold
   with the module as C: three agents were building and testing against
   `crustify/builds` while this switch ran. A build configured from the integration
   worktree's `c/` instead is bound to a tree that is purged once the module integrates,
   and its build files then name sources that no longer exist.
2. **Campaign mode cannot build the Rust library the C links.** The C consumers link "the
   safe crate's Rust static library, built in campaign mode so that it carries no C of its
   own", but campaign mode (`bindgen`, Build modes) requires the variant's artifacts and
   static archive, which exist only once the C has linked, and the C's link needs the Rust
   library first. Once the C links it, the link edges campaign mode reads list it among
   their libraries, so the Rust tests would link the Rust twice, once from their rlib and once
   from the library.
== export-panic-without-a-failure-outcome
# An export whose failure needs an outcome a panic cannot give

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent works around: `porting-symbols`' Functions section has a panic caught at an
export's gateway "reported as a failure, or aborts where the function cannot fail", and a
function can fail through a convention that a panic leaves no way to follow.

## Evidence

`wave-186/batch-5/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) exported `cli_opt_parse` and
`cli_opt_parser_next`. Both report their failures through a status and the outcome they write
to the caller's `cli_opt`: the CLI's commands then call `cli_opt_usage_error(cmd, opts,
&invalid_opt)`, which describes that outcome, its spec and argument. A panic in the parse
leaves no outcome to write: a zeroed one with a failing status would make the CLI print
`unknown option: (null)` for an argument that was never unknown. Both gateways abort on a
panic instead, documented on each. `cli_opt_foreach`, whose failure is a bare non-zero
`int` its caller (`common.c`) only tests, reports a panic as `-1`. The rule, read literally,
asks for the failure in all three; the batch departed from it for two.

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols`, Functions, the panic sentence.

script beside it, as `authoring` places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by

makes the private build dir with an archive lacking them, runs the workspace's tests with
the module's export feature on against it, and, where the target builds C test
executables, relinks them against the crate's static library in place of the module's
objects and runs the suites tied to the module and to the modules that call its exports.

#!/bin/bash
# Build the safe crate's Rust static library for a variant's own C to link (crustify's
# porting-workflow skill, Builds): once a module has switched from C, the remaining C, its
# library, CLI and tests, reaches the module through the crate's exports, and its CMake
# build links this library (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`).
#
#   rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>
#
# Run from the variant's build dir, configured and not yet built, as the first step of its
# `build` command in crustify/artifacts/build.json; <archive> is the library written,
# relative to the build dir, as its configure's `-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names it. The crate
# is the one of the checkout this script belongs to, built as a `staticlib` on the dev
# profile, the campaign's tests' own, in campaign mode against this build dir
# (`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`) with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB` set, so that it reads the build's headers
# and configuration and links none of its C, and with the `bindgen` feature, so that the
# committed bindings are checked against them. Its Rust is instrumented as
# crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh instruments <variant>'s, so that one runtime serves the C
# and the Rust of every C consumer. Cargo's target dir is the build's own, `crustify/cargo`;
# the archive is replaced atomically, so that a link never reads a partial one.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>'
variant=${1:?$usage}
archive=${2:?$usage}
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "$usage" >&2; exit 2; }
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[ -f CMakeCache.txt ] && [ -f build.ninja ] || {
  echo "rust-staticlib.sh: $PWD is not a configured CMake build with the Ninja generator" >&2
  exit 2
}
build=$(pwd -P)
case $archive in /*) ;; *) archive=$build/$archive ;; esac

export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$build CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB=1
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$build/crustify/cargo
crate=(-p libgit2-crustify --lib --locked --features bindgen)
bundled=
case $variant in
  plain)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  coverage|asan-ubsan|tsan)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$host/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  bsan)
    # `cargo bsan` drives `build`, `run` and `test` only, and a `build` cannot change a
    # crate's type. It sets its rustc driver up and runs the cargo CARGO names, so a stand-in
    # for that cargo turns its `build` into `rustc --crate-type staticlib`, every other call,
    # its `metadata` among them, passing through. The /opt shim of `cargo bsan` sets CARGO
    # itself, so the real cargo-bsan, the ELF on PATH, is run directly, as the shim runs it.
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/bsan/$host/debug
    real_cargo=$(type -P cargo)
    real_bsan=
    for c in $(type -ap cargo-bsan); do
      [ "$(head -c4 "$c")" = $'\x7fELF' ] && { real_bsan=$c; break; }
    done
    [ -n "$real_bsan" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no cargo-bsan executable on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
    mkdir -p "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"
    shim=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/cargo-rustc-staticlib
    printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' \

# `cli_opt_status_fprint`'s export writes an interrupted piece again, and reports success

- **finding**: `equiv/status-export-rewrites-an-interrupted-write`
- **batch**: `wave-186/batch-6/run-1`, the review of `git2/src/cli/opt.c`'s `symbol` route
  (batches 1, 4 and 5).
- **item**: `fn::cli_opt_status_fprint`: its export in `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`'s `ffi_export`,
  which writes `OptRef::write_status`'s pieces through `FileWriter`, an `io::Write` over the C
  stream (`wave-186/batch-4`, `64431c07a`).
- **affected commit**: `17401d831`, the wave's tip; since `64431c07a`.
- **class**: an equivalence defect of an export, which the CLI's remaining C (`main.c`'s and
  `opt_usage.c`'s `cli_opt_status_fprint(stderr, …)`) reaches once the module switches from C.

## Finding

C's `cli_opt_status_fprint` writes its message in a few `fprintf` calls and returns at the first
that fails. `fprintf` does not retry a write that a signal interrupts: when the `write` under it
fails with `EINTR` part way through, `fprintf` returns -1, with `errno` `EINTR`, and the bytes
that went out stay out.

The export wrote each piece with `io::Write::write_all`, which `FileWriter` did not implement: the
trait's own `write_all` calls `write` again, from the start of what is left, whenever it fails
with `io::ErrorKind::Interrupted`, the kind of `EINTR`. `FileWriter::write` was one `fprintf` of
the whole piece (`FileRef::print`), which reports an `EINTR` failure as that kind, so the piece
was written a second time, whole, after the part that had gone out, and the message went on to
its end: the export returned 0 where C returns -1, and the stream held the interrupted piece's
first bytes twice. The task's move onto `FileRef::write_all`, a `write` over it alone, keeps the
defect, since `write_all` reports `EINTR` as the same kind.

## Evidence

`src/main.rs` here compiles C's `opt.c` under other names (`build.rs`, `c_cli_opt_*`) beside the
safe crate's exports, which its export feature links in place of the variant's `opt.c`, and
calls each `cli_opt_status_fprint`, the export through its raw binding as C calls it, on a
`fopencookie` stream, unbuffered, whose first write takes three bytes and fails with `EINTR`.
From the repository root:

```text
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=crustify/tmp/target-repro crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh plain run -q \
  --manifest-path crustify/reviews/modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/wave-186/batch-6/equiv/status-export-rewrites-an-interrupted-write/Cargo.toml
```

On `17401d831` it exits 1 (`run-affected.log`):

```text
C:      returned -1, errno 4, wrote "git"
export: returned 0, errno 4, wrote "gitgit2: unknown option: --nope\n"
the export departs from C
```

## Fix

`FileWriter` writes through `FileRef::write_all` (glibc-crustify `24da93f`, pinned by
`ac1f36519`), one `fwrite` of the bytes as they are, and implements `io::Write::write_all` as that
one call, so that a failure ends the message unretried, as it ends C's. Its `write`, which the
export does not call, fails whenever the `fwrite` fails, though part of the bytes may be out:
`write_all` does not report `fwrite`'s count, so no `Ok(n)` can tell how many, and the type's
documentation says so. The same change answers `crustify/evolution/fileref-prints-bytes`: the
argument, the names and the command are written as their bytes, the command through the private
`OptRef::write_status_bytes`, where the export had passed it through `to_string_lossy`.

The reproducer exits 0 on the fix (`run-fixed.log`): both return -1, with `errno` `EINTR`, having
written `git`. It becomes the inline equivalence test
`ffi_import::equiv_priv::an_interrupted_write_fails_both_and_is_written_once`, which compares
C's `cli_opt_status_fprint` with `write_status_bytes` through `FileWriter`, as the export calls
them, with and without a command. It fails on the old `FileWriter`, and on one whose `write` calls
`FileRef::write_all` without overriding `write_all`, and passes on the fix.

API stability: no public item changes.

 ['config', 'user.name'], ['config', '--list'], ['-c', 'user.name=X', 'config', 'user.name'], ['config', '-c', 'user.name=Y', 'user.name'],
 ['-cuser.name=Z', 'config', 'user.name'], ['--config-env=user.name=ENVV', 'config', 'user.name'], ['config', '--config-env', 'user.name=ENVV', 'user.name'],
 ['--no-pager', 'config', 'user.name'], ['config'], ['config', '--get'], ['config', '--nope'],
 ['blame'], ['blame', 'f1'], ['blame', '--nope', 'f1'], ['commit', '--help'], ['commit', '-m'], ['clone'], ['clone', '--help'], ['index-pack'], ['index-pack', '--help'],
 ['cat-file', '-h'], ['hash-object', '--help', '--nope'], ['-c'], ['--config-env'], ['help', '--nope'],
]
def setup(d):
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=d, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1', GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='a', GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='a@b', GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='a', GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='a@b')
    subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', d], check=True, env=env)
    for n, t in (('f1', 'one\n'), ('f2', 'two\n')):
        open(d + '/' + n, 'w').write(t)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, 'add', 'f1', 'f2'], check=True, env=env)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, 'commit', '-qm', 'c'], check=True, env=env)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, 'config', 'user.name', 'Cfg'], check=True, env=env)
    return env
out = []
for i, args in enumerate(cases):
    res = []
    for name, exe in (('C', stock), ('Rust', rust)):
        d = f'{base}/{name}/{i}'
        env = setup(d); env['ENVV'] = 'FromEnv'; env['PAGER'] = 'cat'; env['GIT_PAGER'] = 'cat'
        r = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=d, env=env, input=b'stdin data\n', capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        listing = sorted(os.listdir(d))
        res.append((r.returncode, r.stdout.decode('latin1').replace(d, '<d>'), r.stderr.decode('latin1').replace(d, '<d>'), listing))
    same = res[0] == res[1]
    out.append({'args': args, 'same': same, 'C': res[0], 'Rust': res[1]})
    print(('same   ' if same else 'DIFFER ') + ' '.join(['git2'] + args) + ('' if same else f'\n   C:    {res[0][0]} {res[0][2][:160]!r} {res[0][1][:80]!r} {res[0][3]}\n   Rust: {res[1][0]} {res[1][2][:160]!r} {res[1][1][:80]!r} {res[1][3]}'))
json.dump(out, open(W + '/crustify/tmp/cli/smoke.json', 'w'), indent=1)
print(sum(o['same'] for o in out), 'of', len(out), 'the same')
EOF

input.content:
# The parser reports the bare `-` as an unknown option, where `getopt` takes it as an operand

- **finding**: `logic/bare-dash-is-an-operand`
- **batch**: `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass of `git2/src/cli/opt.c`.
- **item**: `fn::cli_opt_parser_next`, `ParserMut::parse_next` in `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, and
  through it `fn::cli_opt_parse` (`parse`) and `fn::cli_opt_foreach` (`for_each`), and their
  exports (`wave-186/batch-5`, `c62dee857`; the short-option lookup `find_short` is
  `wave-186/batch-4`'s, `64431c07a`).
- **affected commit**: `961150dd9`, the wave's tip; since `c62dee857`.
- **class**: a logic defect of the native API, which the CLI's remaining C reaches through the
  exports once the module switches from C.

## Finding

`parse_next` dispatched every argument that starts with `-`, and is not a literal, to the
short-option parser. For the bare `-`, `find_short` finds no option character, so the parse
reported `Status::UnknownOption`, and `parse` failed on it, in either style.

The specification the parser implements takes the bare `-` as an operand:

- POSIX `getopt` (XSH, `getopt`): "If, when `getopt()` is called, `argv[optind]` ... points to
  the string `"-"`, `getopt()` shall return -1 without changing `optind`": it is the first
  operand, not an option. POSIX's Utility Syntax Guideline 13 gives it its meaning, standard
  input, where a utility takes files.
- GNU `getopt_long`, which `opt.h` names as the style of `CLI_OPT_PARSE_GNU` ("Parse with GNU
  `getopt_long` style behavior, where options can be intermixed with arguments"), takes it as a
  non-option argument, which it permutes as it permutes any other.
- git's own `parse-options`, whose commands the CLI's mirror, takes it as a non-option argument
  (`parse_options_step`: `if (*arg != '-' || !arg[1])`): `git init -` creates a repository in
  the directory `-`, and `git blame -` looks the path `-` up.

The port departed from all three. The C departs too, differently: `spec_for_short` compares the
empty option character with every spec's alias, so the bare `-` selects the table's first spec
without one, and `parse_short` and `spec_for_sort` then read the byte after the argument's end.
Batch 4 corrected that read, by matching no spec, and the bare `-` became unknown; batch 6 left
the choice to this pass. Nothing in the module's documentation, its tests or a command of the
CLI gives the bare `-` an option's meaning, and its departure from the cited specifications was
never weighed.

## Evidence

`src/main.rs` here parses, through the safe API alone (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`), `-`, `-q -`
and `- -q` against a table of a `-q` bool and one argument spec, in the default style and
`FORCE_GNU`, and asserts what `getopt` gives: the argument spec takes `-`, and `-q` is set where
given. From the repository root:

```text
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=crustify/tmp/target-repro crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh plain run -q \
  --manifest-path crustify/reviews/modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/wave-186/batch-7/logic/bare-dash-is-an-operand/Cargo.toml
```

On `961150dd9` it exits 1 (`run-affected.log`):

```text
["-"] ParseFlags(0): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-"] ParseFlags(2): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-q", "-"] ParseFlags(0): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-", "-q"] ParseFlags(2): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
the bare `-` is not taken as an operand
```

What the CLI shows, from the plain variant's `git2` and the same executable relinked with the
exports in place of `opt.c.o` (this batch's scratch check, Notes): `git2 init -` printed the
usage and exited 0 under C, having taken `-` as `--help`, and `git2 hash-object -` likewise;
the exports, before this fix, report `unknown option: -` with the usage.

## Fix

`parse_next` takes the bare `-` as a bare argument, before the short-option branch: it takes the
next argument spec, or is unknown once those are taken, as any bare argument is, and a GNU-style
parse keeps it among the bare arguments it moves options ahead of, as `find_for_sort` already
selected no spec for it. The documentation of `parse_next`, of the module, and the C defect it
lists say so. The reproducer exits 0 on the fix (`run-fixed.log`).

It becomes the `unit_pub` test `cli::opt::a_bare_dash_is_a_bare_argument`, which replaces
`a_bare_dash_is_unknown`, the test that asserted the departure: `-` alone, after an option and
before one GNU style moves, in both styles, and unknown once the argument spec is taken. The
gateway's test `a_bare_dash_reaches_the_command_as_an_argument` checks it through
`cli_opt_parse`. With the exports linked into the CLI, `git2 init -` creates the repository
`-/.git`, as `git init -` does, `git2 hash-object -` reports that it cannot find `-`, and
`git2 -` reports `'-' is not a git2 command`, exit 1. The stock C prints `unknown option: -`
there, exit 129, but reaches it by reading the bytes past the argument as further options;
git's own top level, which is not `getopt`, reports `unknown option: -`.

API stability: no item's signature changes; `parse_next`, `parse` and `for_each` accept the
bare `-` as an argument, which they refused, a behaviour change recorded in the batch's Notes.

# The parser reports the bare `-` as an unknown option, where `getopt` takes it as an operand

- **finding**: `logic/bare-dash-is-an-operand`
- **batch**: `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass of `git2/src/cli/opt.c`.
- **item**: `fn::cli_opt_parser_next`, `ParserMut::parse_next` in `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, and
  through it `fn::cli_opt_parse` (`parse`) and `fn::cli_opt_foreach` (`for_each`), and their
  exports (`wave-186/batch-5`, `c62dee857`; the short-option lookup `find_short` is
  `wave-186/batch-4`'s, `64431c07a`).
- **affected commit**: `961150dd9`, the wave's tip; since `c62dee857`.
- **class**: a logic defect of the native API, which the CLI's remaining C reaches through the
  exports once the module switches from C.

## Finding

`parse_next` dispatched every argument that starts with `-`, and is not a literal, to the
short-option parser. For the bare `-`, `find_short` finds no option character, so the parse
reported `Status::UnknownOption`, and `parse` failed on it, in either style.

The specification the parser implements takes the bare `-` as an operand:

- POSIX `getopt` (XSH, `getopt`): "If, when `getopt()` is called, `argv[optind]` ... points to
  the string `"-"`, `getopt()` shall return -1 without changing `optind`": it is the first
  operand, not an option. POSIX's Utility Syntax Guideline 13 gives it its meaning, standard
  input, where a utility takes files.
- GNU `getopt_long`, which `opt.h` names as the style of `CLI_OPT_PARSE_GNU` ("Parse with GNU
  `getopt_long` style behavior, where options can be intermixed with arguments"), takes it as a
  non-option argument, which it permutes as it permutes any other.
- git's own `parse-options`, whose commands the CLI's mirror, takes it as a non-option argument
  (`parse_options_step`: `if (*arg != '-' || !arg[1])`): `git init -` creates a repository in
  the directory `-`, and `git blame -` looks the path `-` up.

The port departed from all three. The C departs too, differently: `spec_for_short` compares the
empty option character with every spec's alias, so the bare `-` selects the table's first spec
without one, and `parse_short` and `spec_for_sort` then read the byte after the argument's end.
Batch 4 corrected that read, by matching no spec, and the bare `-` became unknown; batch 6 left
the choice to this pass. Nothing in the module's documentation, its tests or a command of the
CLI gives the bare `-` an option's meaning, and its departure from the cited specifications was
never weighed.

## Evidence

`src/main.rs` here parses, through the safe API alone (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`), `-`, `-q -`
and `- -q` against a table of a `-q` bool and one argument spec, in the default style and
`FORCE_GNU`, and asserts what `getopt` gives: the argument spec takes `-`, and `-q` is set where
given. From the repository root:

```text
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=crustify/tmp/target-repro crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh plain run -q \
  --manifest-path crustify/reviews/modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/wave-186/batch-7/logic/bare-dash-is-an-operand/Cargo.toml
```

On `961150dd9` it exits 1 (`run-affected.log`):

```text
["-"] ParseFlags(0): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-"] ParseFlags(2): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-q", "-"] ParseFlags(0): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-", "-q"] ParseFlags(2): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
the bare `-` is not taken as an operand
```

What the CLI shows, from the plain variant's `git2` and the same executable relinked with the
exports in place of `opt.c.o` (this batch's scratch check, Notes): `git2 init -` printed the
usage and exited 0 under C, having taken `-` as `--help`, and `git2 hash-object -` likewise;
the exports, before this fix, report `unknown option: -` with the usage.

## Fix

`parse_next` takes the bare `-` as a bare argument, before the short-option branch: it takes the
next argument spec, or is unknown once those are taken, as any bare argument is, and a GNU-style
parse keeps it among the bare arguments it moves options ahead of, as `find_for_sort` already
selected no spec for it. The documentation of `parse_next`, of the module, and the C defect it
lists say so. The reproducer exits 0 on the fix (`run-fixed.log`).

It becomes the `unit_pub` test `cli::opt::a_bare_dash_is_a_bare_argument`, which replaces
`a_bare_dash_is_unknown`, the test that asserted the departure: `-` alone, after an option and
before one GNU style moves, in both styles, and unknown once the argument spec is taken. The
gateway's test `a_bare_dash_reaches_the_command_as_an_argument` checks it through
`cli_opt_parse`. With the exports linked into the CLI, `git2 init -` creates the repository
`-/.git`, as `git init -` does, `git2 hash-object -` reports that it cannot find `-`, and
`git2 -` reports `'-' is not a git2 command`, exit 1. The stock C prints `unknown option: -`
there, exit 129, but reaches it by reading the bytes past the argument as further options;
git's own top level, which is not `getopt`, reports `unknown option: -`.

API stability: no item's signature changes; `parse_next`, `parse` and `for_each` accept the
bare `-` as an argument, which they refused, a behaviour change recorded in the batch's Notes.

# The `char **` an `Args` spec stores for C is derived from a borrow that ends with the call

- **finding**: `ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow`
- **batch**: `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass of `git2/src/cli/opt.c`.
- **item**: `fn::cli_opt_parse`, and `fn::cli_opt_parser_next` and `fn::cli_opt_foreach`: their
  exports in `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`'s `ffi_export` (`wave-186/batch-5`, `c62dee857`), over
  `take_bare` (`fn::parse_arg`), which stores an `Args` spec's position, and `Parser::into_args`.
- **affected commit**: `961150dd9`, the wave's tip; since `c62dee857`.
- **class**: undefined behaviour reached from C through an export, within `opt.h`'s contract, as
  Miri's default aliasing model, Stacked Borrows, defines it: the campaign's Miri gate.

## Finding

A `CLI_OPT_TYPE_ARGS` spec's variable is a `char **`, which C reads after the parse:
`cmd_hash_object.c` walks `filenames` to `argv`'s `NULL`. The C parse stores `&args[idx]`, its
caller's own pointer plus an index. The export adopted `argv + 1` as a `&mut [Arg]`, and
`take_bare` stored the position from a shared reborrow of it,
`ArgsSlot::set(parser.as_ref().args().get(idx..))`: a pointer that grants access only while no
later borrow of the array takes it away. Two do, before C reads it:

- `parse` itself, which hands its array back through `Parser::into_args`, a
  `slice::from_raw_parts_mut` over it: a unique reborrow, which invalidates the stored pointer
  before `cli_opt_parse` returns; and
- any later export over the same `argv`, whose adoption is a unique reborrow of the array:
  `cmd_hash_object.c -w` opens the repository, and `common.c`'s `parse_common_options` parses
  `argv + 1` again through `cli_opt_foreach`, before the files are walked.

C then reads `argv` through a pointer whose access Rust ended. Under Tree Borrows the same run is
accepted, since neither reborrow writes the array here; Stacked Borrows, Miri's default and the
model of the campaign's Miri gate, reports it. Once the module switches, the gateway's tests run
under that gate, and the C that walks the variable is the CLI's.

`cli_opt_parser_init` had the same shape for the parser's own `args`: it stored the adopted
slice's pointer, not C's, so that a position `cli_opt_parser_next` stored was derived from a
borrow too. `main.c`'s parser never reaches its `Args` spec, since it stops at the command.

## Evidence

`src/main.rs` here runs `cmd_hash_object.c`'s sequence, calling each export through its raw
binding as the C does, within `opt.h`'s contract: `cli_opt_parse` of `hash-object a.txt -w
b.txt` against `-w` and a required `Args` spec, then `cli_opt_foreach` of the same `argv + 1`
against `-c`, then the walk of the `char **` to `argv`'s `NULL`. Under Miri, which resolves the
raw bindings to the exports, from the repository root:

```text
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=crustify/tmp/target-miri-repro cargo +nightly-2026-10-08 miri run -q \
  --manifest-path crustify/reviews/modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/wave-186/batch-7/ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow/Cargo.toml
```

On `961150dd9` it exits 1 (`run-affected.log`):

```text
error: Undefined Behavior: attempting a read access using <8387> at alloc1467[0x10], but that tag does not exist in the borrow stack for this location
  --> src/main.rs:78:29
78 |         let file = unsafe { at.read() };
help: <8387> was created by a SharedReadOnly retag at offsets [0x10..0x20]
  --> src/main.rs:53:9
53 |         sys::cli_opt_parse(opt.as_mut_ptr(), specs.as_ptr().cast(), args, len, sys::CLI_OPT_PARSE_GNU)
help: <8387> was later invalidated at offsets [0x8..0x20] by a Unique retag
  --> src/main.rs:53:9
```

The tag is the one `take_bare` stored (`ArgsSlot::set`, `opt.rs:649`), and the unique retag
`Parser::into_args`'s (`opt.rs:2622`), as the gateway test that found it showed with the
crate's own frames. With `MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-tree-borrows` the run exits 0
(`run-affected-tree-borrows.log`).

## Fix

The gateway hands C its own pointers. `rebase_args_slots`, run by `cli_opt_parse`,
`cli_opt_parser_next` and `cli_opt_foreach` once the parse step is done, rewrites each position
stored in an `Args` spec's variable of the table, when it lies within the array C passed, as C's
pointer plus its index, the `&args[idx]` C stores; a position outside it, written by an earlier
parse of another array, is left alone. `cli_opt_parser_init` stores C's `args` in the parser, as
C does, over the adopted slice's, so that `cli_opt_parser_next` rebases onto it. The native API
does not change: its positions are never read through, and `ArgsSlot::get_in` compares
addresses alone. The reproducer exits 0 on the fix (`run-fixed.log`).

It becomes the gateway's test
`ffi_export::unit_priv::the_files_a_parse_stores_outlive_a_later_parse_of_its_argv`, which runs
the same sequence through the exports and walks the files. Under Miri it fails on the old
gateway, with the same report, and passes on the fix. It compiles with the export feature,
as the gateway does, until the switch deletes the feature; from then on it runs in `lib`, and in
the Miri gate.

API stability: no public item changes.

For: libgit2-crustify's issue tracker (https://github.com/crustify-rs/libgit2-crustify/issues),
as a public issue. The defect is in the crate's own Rust export, not in libgit2, and has no
security impact we know of: a status message written twice to standard error.

Title: `cli_opt_status_fprint`'s export writes a piece again after `EINTR`, and reports success

### Summary

The Rust export of the CLI's `cli_opt_status_fprint` (`src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, under the
`ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c` feature) writes the message's pieces with `io::Write::write_all` over
a C stream. Its writer left `write_all` to the trait's default, which retries a write that fails
with `ErrorKind::Interrupted`:

```rust
impl io::Write for FileWriter<'_> {
    fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
        /* one fprintf(stream, "%s", text) of the whole piece */
    }
}
```

When the `write(2)` under a piece fails with `EINTR` after part of it went out, C's `fprintf`
returns -1 and `cli_opt_status_fprint` returns that failure; the export writes the whole piece
again, finishes the message and returns 0.

### Reproduction

On a `fopencookie` stream, unbuffered, whose first write takes three bytes and fails with
`EINTR`, for an unknown option `--nope` and the command `git2`:

```text
C:      returned -1, errno 4, wrote "git"
export: returned 0, errno 4, wrote "gitgit2: unknown option: --nope\n"
```

The reproducer, a small Cargo package that runs both, is available on request.

### Fix

Fixed in `wave-186/batch-6/run-1`: the writer writes through glibc-bindings'
`FileRef::write_all`, one `fwrite` per piece, and implements `write_all` as that one call, so
that a failure ends the message as it ends C's. A patch is available.

Found by [Crustify](https://github.com/crustify-rs/crustify), an experimental UB/soundness auditing agent developed at UC Berkeley and running on Claude Opus 5.5, then manually reviewed and independently reproduced.

For: libgit2-crustify's issue tracker (https://github.com/crustify-rs/libgit2-crustify/issues),
as a public issue. The defect is in the crate's own Rust port of the CLI's option parser, and
has no security impact we know of: a command-line argument refused.

Title: the ported option parser refuses the bare `-`, which `getopt` takes as an operand

### Summary

The Rust port of the CLI's `src/cli/opt.c` (`src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`) parses every argument
that starts with `-` as a short option, the bare `-` included, and reports it as an unknown
option:

```rust
if in_short || (bytes.starts_with(b"-") && !in_literal) {
    return take_short(self);
}
```

POSIX `getopt` returns at `"-"` without consuming it, as the first operand; GNU `getopt_long`,
whose style `opt.h` names, and git's `parse-options` take it as a non-option argument, so that
`git init -` creates the directory `-`. libgit2's own C parser matches the bare `-` with the
first spec that has no alias and reads past the argument's end, so `git2 init -` prints the
usage; the port corrected that read, but refused the argument.

### Reproduction

Parsing against a table of a `-q` flag and one argument spec:

```text
["-"] ParseFlags(0): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
["-", "-q"] ParseFlags(2): argument None, failure Some((Some(UnknownOption), Some("-")))
```

The reproducer, a small Cargo package using the safe API alone, is available on request.

### Fix

Fixed in `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`: the bare `-` is a bare argument, in either style. A patch is
available.

Found by [Crustify](https://github.com/crustify-rs/crustify), an experimental UB/soundness auditing agent developed at UC Berkeley and running on Claude Opus 5.5, then manually reviewed and independently reproduced.
EOF

as a public issue. The defect is in the crate's own Rust exports of the CLI's option parser,
not in libgit2; it is undefined behaviour under Miri's Stacked Borrows model, with no
miscompilation or security impact we know of.

Title: `cli_opt_parse`'s export stores a `char **` for C derived from a borrow that ends first

### Summary

The Rust exports of the CLI's `src/cli/opt.c` (`src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs`, under the
`ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c` feature) adopt the `argv` C passes as a `&mut [Arg]`. A
`CLI_OPT_TYPE_ARGS` spec's variable, a `char **` that C walks after the parse, was stored from a
shared reborrow of that slice:

```rust
slot.set(parser.as_ref().args().get(idx..).unwrap_or_default());
```

The parse's own `slice::from_raw_parts_mut` over the array, and the next export's adoption of
the same `argv`, as `common.c`'s `cli_opt_foreach` does for `hash-object -w`, are unique
reborrows, which end that pointer's access before C reads through it.

### Reproduction

`cli_opt_parse` of `hash-object a.txt -w b.txt`, `cli_opt_foreach` of the same `argv + 1`, then
the walk of the variable, each export called through its C declaration, under Miri:

```text
error: Undefined Behavior: attempting a read access using <8387> at alloc1467[0x10], but that tag does not exist in the borrow stack for this location
help: <8387> was created by a SharedReadOnly retag at offsets [0x10..0x20]
help: <8387> was later invalidated at offsets [0x8..0x20] by a Unique retag
```

Tree Borrows accepts the run. The reproducer, a small Cargo package, is available on request.

### Fix

Fixed in `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`: the exports store C's own pointer plus the position's index,
as the C does, and the parser keeps C's `argv` pointer. A patch is available.

Found by [Crustify](https://github.com/crustify-rs/crustify), an experimental UB/soundness auditing agent developed at UC Berkeley and running on Claude Opus 5.5, then manually reviewed and independently reproduced.
EOF

set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:

## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

input.content:
### `git2/src/cli/opt.c` wave 186 batch 7: module pass

The module pass over `src/git2/src/cli/opt.rs` and the module's four test files, the
module's whole `port` across its folded waves (186 to 193): the four enums, the three structs
kept in their C layouts (`wrap`, until waves 1988 and 2404), 21 symbols and the five exports
under `ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c`, off. It ran every objective, `fix` included. The module
switches from C right after this pass, so its unsafe regions, its exports and the structs'
layouts were reviewed for what the CLI's remaining C relies on: `main.c` steps a parser over
`argv + 1` GNU style and reads `optparser.idx` to move the command ahead, the `cmd_*.c` build
their tables as `const cli_opt_spec[]` and read their variables, `cmd_hash_object.c` walking
its `Args` spec's `char **` to `argv`'s `NULL`, `common.c`'s `parse_option` reads each outcome's
spec, alias and value through `cli_opt_foreach`, and `opt_usage.c` and `main.c` describe a
failure through `cli_opt_status_fprint`. The layouts are bindgen's, asserted field by field
against `opt.h`, and the handles are `#[repr(transparent)]` over them. It filed two reports,
both fixed:

- `ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow` (reproducer, Miri). The position an
  `Args` spec stores for C was taken from a shared reborrow of the `argv` the export adopted
  as a `&mut [Arg]`, and `Parser::into_args`'s unique reborrow, or the next export's adoption
  of the same `argv`, as `cmd_hash_object.c -w`'s `common.c` makes, ended its access before C
  walked it. Stacked Borrows, Miri's default, reports the walk; Tree Borrows accepts it. The
  gateway now rewrites each such position as C's own pointer plus its index
  (`rebase_args_slots`, after `cli_opt_parse`, `cli_opt_parser_next` and `cli_opt_foreach`),
  and `cli_opt_parser_init` stores C's `args` in the parser, as C does. Its regression test is
  the gateway's `the_files_a_parse_stores_outlive_a_later_parse_of_its_argv`, which fails under
  Miri without the rewrite.
- `logic/bare-dash-is-an-operand` (reproducer). The bare `-` was an unknown option, batch 4's
  correction of the C's read past it, which batch 6 left to this pass. POSIX `getopt`, GNU
  `getopt_long`, which `opt.h` names, and git's `parse-options` take it as an operand: it is
  now a bare argument, in either style, documented on `parse_next` and the module, and
  `a_bare_dash_is_a_bare_argument` replaces `a_bare_dash_is_unknown`. After the switch, `git2
  init -` creates `-/.git`, as `git init -` does, where the C printed the usage and exited 0,
  and `git2 -` reports `'-' is not a git2 command`, exit 1, where the C printed `unknown
  option: -`, exit 129, after reading the bytes past the argument; git's top level, which is
  not `getopt`, reports `unknown option: -`. That message is the one change the CLI shows.

The seven C defects batches 4 to 6 did not carry over were weighed again, each a documented,
tested correction, none an `equiv` finding; the bare `-` was the one left open, and is the
logic finding above. The other objectives found nothing. `unsafety`: the one public `unsafe fn`
is `SpecTable::from_ptr`, an adoption no safe variant replaces. `contracts`: each gateway's
`# Safety` asks what `main.c`, the commands and `common.c` give, the gateway's two new raw
accesses included; `Option<Arg>` over a `char *` holds by the null-pointer guarantee of a
`#[repr(transparent)]` `NonNull`. `ub` on the safe and unsafe APIs: the handles' borrows hold,
and the positions are never read through in Rust. `equiv`, `idiom`, `ergonomics`,
`conventions`: none. `test-adequacy`: the gateway had no test of its own, and the `equiv`
tests that checked it in the batches' scratch links retire with the C. Its region gains six
`unit_priv` tests, written after the C that calls each export: `main.c`'s loop to its command
and the parser's position, a command's parse of its `argv` in place with its failures and the
`char **` walked to `NULL`, `common.c`'s callback, the status message of a failed parse, the
bare `-` reaching a command, and the regression test above, each export called by its C name
over C's own forms, its outcome and parser written over scribbled storage. They compile with
the feature, as the gateway does, until the switch, and run in `lib` from then on. Two mutants
fail them (an `init` that ignores its flags, an `Args` slot one past), and the five that call
no C pass under Miri with the feature on.

The module has no C tests: `modules.json`'s `tests` is empty for it, and no suite under
`c/tests` builds or reaches `src/cli`, so the switch's C-test gate checks nothing of the
exports. What checks the CLI's parsing after the switch is the crate's own tests, the
`unit_pub`, `ub_safe` and `ub_unsafe` ones of the native API and the gateway's six, and the CLI
itself. As a scratch check, the plain variant's `git2` was relinked from its `build.ninja`

The module pass is landed on `refs/heads/crustify/waves/wave-186`. The wave branch moved `961150dd9..63a4b8d1d` in two commits: `8261702d7` files the two reports, and `63a4b8d1d` holds the fixes, the new gateway tests, the dashboard cells and Notes, and the run's records. It filed two findings, both now fixed, each with a reproducer that fails on the tip and passes on the fix.

**Findings**
- **`ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow`** (reproduced with Miri). An `Args` spec's variable is a `char **` that C reads after the parse; `cmd_hash_object.c` walks it to `argv`'s `NULL`. The exports stored it from a short-lived Rust borrow of `argv`, and a later borrow (`Parser::into_args`, or `common.c`'s `cli_opt_foreach` over the same `argv` for `hash-object -w`) cancelled its access before C read it.
  - Miri's default model (Stacked Borrows, which the campaign's Miri gate uses) reports the walk as undefined behaviour; the stricter-looking Tree Borrows model accepts it.
  - Fix: the gateway now rewrites each stored position as C's own pointer plus its index, and `cli_opt_parser_init` keeps C's own `argv` pointer. The native API is unchanged.
  - Regression test: `the_files_a_parse_stores_outlive_a_later_parse_of_its_argv`, which fails under Miri without the fix.
- **`logic/bare-dash-is-an-operand`**: I weighed the bare `-` as you asked and changed it. The port had made it an unknown option; POSIX `getopt`, GNU `getopt_long` (the style `opt.h` names) and git's own option parsing all take it as an ordinary argument.
